newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak stats office lowers GDP growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Slovak stats office lowers GDP growth forecast.

text.p: The head of the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) on Wednesday downgraded the bureau's gross domestic product forecast for 1996 to 6.4-7.0 percent from 7.1 percent.

The bureau released a statement listing only its revised forecast of 7.0 percent growth, but SUSR Chairman Stefan Condik warned the central bank could damp down growth if it adopted further restrictive policy measures.

"We forecast real GDP growth within a 6.4-7.0 percent interval by the end of the year, but this will not hold if the central bank starts acting as if the economy was overheating," Condik told a news conference.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) implemented a series of measures in July aimed at tightening money supply.
The moves included rises in the Lombard last-resort lending facility and minimum reserve requirements for banks, which boosted the interbank money market rates to a 13-14 percent.
Condik said the bureau's GDP forecast was also based on a survey of major exporters' and producers' expectations.
"It seems that these (restrictive) central bank measures will remain in force as long as the problem of bad loan portfolios of Slovak banks is not solved," Condik added.
Condik said the latest inflation figures showed that the economy had not reached the stage of overheating. "We still could have waited, the inflation developments favoured that".
Still the lowest in eastern Europe, Slovak consumer price inflation was 5.6 percent year-on-year in August against 5.5 percent in July.
But the key money supply measure, M2, rose 21.0 percent year-on-year in July, compared with a full-year target of 11.6 percent expansion.
